title: Inverse Circular Functions
notes: **Why inverse functions are needed:** sine, cosine and tangent are periodic and many-to-one, so they do not have true inverses unless their domains are restricted.

**Principal value branches:** the restricted domains that make the functions one-to-one: $\sin^{-1}x$ on $[-1,1]$ with range $[-\pi/2, \pi/2]$; $\cos^{-1}x$ on $[-1,1]$ with range $[0, \pi]$; $\tan^{-1}x$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with range $(-\pi/2, \pi/2)$.
confusion: Inverse trigonometric functions are not the same as $1/\sin x$ or $1/\cos x$. $\sin^{-1}x$ means the angle whose sine is $x$, not the reciprocal.
The range of $\sin^{-1}x$ is $[-\pi/2, \pi/2]$, not the full circle. Always check which branch you are in.
universalFacts: Inverse trigonometric functions always return principal values by convention.
The sum of complementary inverse functions (sin and cos, tan and cot) is always $\pi/2$.
